name: Bur Oak Acorn

facts.how: Leached, then eaten or ground to flour

caution: Leach out the tannins in repeated water changes until no bitterness remains before eating any acorn. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Bur oak grows the biggest acorn of any Texas oak, capped in a shaggy fringe. Its size makes shelling and leaching far less tedious.

sections.title: Leaching and flour
sections.body: The lower-tannin acorns of white-oak-group trees like bur oak leach quickly. Grind the sweet result for baking.
